fixture: mfx-0 slider probe (300x20x20 rail, 50x20x20 slide, Assembly Slider joint, LengthMin 0 / LengthMax 250)
engine: FreeCAD 1.1.4 (Revision 20260928, git 4fd3bf320) Assembly Simulation / Motion, headless freecadcmd (extracted AppImage)

mfx0_motion_econ.csv.signal: z (the probe's joint slid the part along world z; x stayed 0; joint_distance is NOT updated by updateForFrame and reads 0.0 mm throughout)
mfx0_motion_econ.csv.t_s_column_caveat: t_s in this file was written as frame / jFramesPerSecond by the probe. That is WRONG for frame 0 and off by one frame for the rest — use frame_time below, never the column.

frame_time.rule: frame 0 = the pre-motion placement (the part exactly where the assembly solve left it, z0 = 20 in the probe); frame f >= 1 is sim time t = (f - 1) * cTimeStepOutput. numberOfFrames = (bTimeEnd - aTimeStart) / cTimeStepOutput + 1 motion frames + 1 pre-motion frame (0-1.5 s at 0.1 -> 16 + 1 = 17; at 0.05 -> 31 + 1 = 32; 0-3.0 s at 0.1 -> 31 + 1 = 32).
frame_time.ramp_explained: There is NO start-up ramp and no solver-internal first step. The apparent ramp in the plan (z = 20, 40 at 't = 0.5', 90 at 't = 1.0', then 10 mm/frame) is exactly z(f) = 100 * (f - 1) * 0.1 read against the mislabelled t_s column: z = 40 is frame 5 = t 0.4 s, z = 90 is frame 10 = t 0.9 s. The jump 20 -> 0 between frame 0 and frame 1 is the part moving from its solved placement (z0 = 20) to the formula's value at t = 0 (0). Frame times are uniform.
evidence_2026-11-03: formula '100*time+30': frames 1.. = 30, 40, 50 ... (frame 1 is t = 0 -> 30, so the offset is the formula, not a ramp)
z0 = 0 placement: frame 0 = 0, frame 1 = 0, frame 2 = 10 ... (no jump when the placement already equals the formula at t = 0)
cTimeStepOutput 0.05: 32 frames, 5 mm per frame; jFramesPerSecond 20: still 17 frames (fps is playback only, it does not sample)
bTimeEnd 3.0: z reaches 300 at frame 31 -> the Motion solver does NOT honour LengthMax 250 (Enable flags set). The joint limit is Polari's hard stop, not FreeCAD's, in the kinematic run.
